overall: The AG found neither the Select Board nor the Planning Board violated the Open Meeting Law on the joint September 11, 2023 meeting notice, executive session purpose, or outside deliberation; the late minutes claim was not reviewed.

allegations.summary: Joint Select Board and Planning Board meeting notice allegedly insufficient to inform the public of the meeting's business.
allegations.key_passage: As such, we find that the single notice of the September 11, 2023, joint meeting was sufficient notice for both public bodies.

allegations.summary: Executive session notice for potential litigation over 1688 Central Avenue allegedly lacked sufficient specificity.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the notice was sufficiently specific where the Board identified the specific litigation matter it planned to discuss during the executive session.

allegations.summary: Select Board allegedly entered executive session under Purpose 3 for an improper purpose, since the litigation was against the Planning Board and the Select Board had no litigating position.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that it was permissible for the Select Board to meet in executive session to discuss whether to appeal the decision of the Land Court.

allegations.summary: Boards allegedly deliberated outside a meeting about whether to schedule the executive session on the pending Land Court matter.
allegations.key_passage: we have not been presented with any evidence that a quorum of members of the Select Board or Planning Board discussed this matter outside of a properly posted meeting.

allegations.summary: On further review, complainant alleged the Planning Board did not create or timely approve minutes of the September 11, 2023 joint meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We find that this allegation was not clearly raised in the original complaint and thus we do not review its merits.
